lessons.title: What time is it?

items.exampleMeaning: What time is it, please?

items.example: Es la una de la tarde.
items.exampleMeaning: It's one o'clock in the afternoon.

items.example: Son las dos de la mañana.
items.exampleMeaning: It's two o'clock in the morning.
We arrive at three o'clock.
At what time does the movie start?
We arrive early at the station.

lessons.tip: In Spanish, use 'es' for one o'clock and 'son' for all other hours. Remember to use 'de la mañana', 'de la tarde', or 'de la noche' for clarity.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: At what time does the train start?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, llegamos temprano a la estación.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, we arrive early at the station.

scenario.partnerRole: A is a friend helping B with transport questions.
scenario.learnerRole: B is learning to ask about the time and schedules.
scenario.brief: You ask your friend about the time and when the train starts. They will answer your questions.
scenario.goal: You need to find out what time the train leaves.

lessons.title: Buying Tickets

items.example: Quisiera un boleto a la ciudad.
items.exampleMeaning: I would like a ticket to the city.
How much is the ticket to Madrid?
Here you go, your ticket.
Where do I buy it, at the station?
I can pay with a card.

items.example: Gracias, muy amable de su parte.
items.exampleMeaning: Thank you, very kind of you.

lessons.tip: When buying tickets, you can use 'quisiera' to sound polite. Always remember to ask '¿Cuánto cuesta?' to know the price.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Quisiera un boleto a la ciudad.
dialogue.meaning: I would like a ticket to the city.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Can I pay with a card?

scenario.partnerRole: A is a ticket seller at a station.
scenario.brief: You need to ask about the price and how to pay for a ticket. The seller will help you.
scenario.goal: You need to buy a ticket to the city.

lessons.title: Using Common Verbs

items.exampleMeaning: I go to the station.
You go to the cinema.
We go to the park.
I take the bus.
You take a taxi.
We take the train.

lessons.tip: The verb 'ir' means 'to go'. Use 'voy' for 'I go', 'vas' for 'you go', and 'vamos' for 'we go'. These are very common in daily conversation.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Are you going to the cinema?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: No, I go to the station.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Shall we go to the park?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: Yes, we go to the park.

scenario.partnerRole: A is a friend discussing plans with B.
scenario.brief: You want to talk about going places and taking transport. Your friend will ask you questions.
scenario.goal: You need to explain where you are going.

lessons.title: Asking About Schedules

items.meaning: At what time does it leave?
items.exampleMeaning: At what time does the train leave?

items.example: El autobús sale a las cinco.
items.exampleMeaning: The bus leaves at five o'clock.
How long does the trip take?
The trip takes two hours.
The train is fast.
The bus is comfortable.

lessons.tip: To ask about schedules, use '¿A qué hora sale?' for departure times. 'Dura' is used to ask about how long something takes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: At what time does the train leave?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: How long does the trip take?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, el tren es rápido y cómodo.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, the train is fast and comfortable.

scenario.learnerRole: B is asking about train schedules.
scenario.brief: You need to inquire about train departure times and travel duration. The agent will provide information.
scenario.goal: You need to understand the train schedule.
